scene_description: A small bright office with a window blind, low wooden cubby shelf, floor lamp, two wheeled chairs, a table, a paneled door, and a foreground plant.
initial_target_observations: Both initial chairs have visible central stems and wheeled bases beneath their curved seats. Their support connections appear generally continuous in the image, although parts are small or occluded.
candidate_target_observations: The chair near the shelf has a visible central stem connecting the seat region to a wheeled base. The foreground chair's lower support is obscured by the table and plant or cropped from view, so its connection cannot be assessed. The reference shows both chairs' stems and wheeled bases more clearly.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The visible chair support in the candidate looks plausible in projection, but the second chair's support is not visible enough to judge. The door, shelf and lamp remain recognizable; RGB projections do not establish actual mesh contact or collision.
new_visible_defects: The candidate framing hides the foreground chair's base and most of the table, reducing visibility of the office furniture compared with the initial view. This is an occlusion and framing difference, not evidence that the support is absent.
other_changes: The candidate moves to a higher, closer viewpoint, placing the table mostly out of frame and showing the door more obliquely. The reference has a darker wood-textured floor and tabletop, more strongly modeled chairs, and a dark open-looking door; both reconstructions are flatter and paler. The candidate's blind and shelf remain broadly similar to the initial reconstruction, but the altered view makes direct size and alignment comparisons uncertain.

evidence.description: Both chairs have visible central posts and wheeled bases, with some base parts near the frame edge.
Both chair seats have visible stems and wheeled bases.
The chair by the shelf has a visible stem and wheeled base.
The second chair's lower portion is hidden by foreground objects or outside the frame.
The dark paneled door is shown at an angle, with a prominent leaf silhouette.
The table and its legs are largely visible.
Only parts of the foreground tabletop are visible in the closer framing.

uncertainty: No specific intervention target was identified. Chair support visibility is a relevant comparison, but different viewpoints and occlusion prevent determining whether the hidden support changed or whether any underlying geometry was corrected. Material and spatial comparisons are also affected by lighting and framing.
